riskReasons: The accepted hyphenated name and Acer palmatum placement are supported.
The characteristic narrow-lobed linearilobum foliage is consistent across the reviewed sources.
Near-name cultivars and an informal nickname require explicit separation but do not create an identity dispute.

duplicateCheck.notes: Compared with all RC-001–RC-010 records and all other approved Catalogue assignments. It is not RC-002 ‘Seiryu’: ‘Koto-no-ito’ has linearilobum strap-like lobes rather than an upright dissectum leaf. ‘Yamato-koto-no-ito’ and ‘Koto-ito-komachi’ remain separate near-name cultivars. C0 resolves as unique.

identityNotes: The Atlas uses the RHS accepted hyphenated form ‘Koto-no-ito’. Spaced and title-case forms are retained only as search variants. ‘Yamato-koto-no-ito’ and ‘Koto-ito-komachi’ are separate near-names, not synonyms. The Seattle Japanese Garden nickname ‘Dancing Monkey Tree’ is not treated as a cultivar synonym.

content.summary: A slow-growing, rounded Japanese maple valued for exceptionally narrow, thread-like green leaf lobes that move lightly in the wind and turn orange-yellow in autumn.
content.habit: Rounded, bushy, semi-dwarf shrub or small tree with graceful branching; RHS places the usual mature range around 1.5–2.5 m, while descriptive text allows development toward about 3 m over time.
content.leafForm: Linearilobum foliage with five to seven long, narrow, tapering lobes. A Seattle Japanese Garden account notes very fine spring leaves on older wood and somewhat broader, though still narrow, leaves on later new growth.

seasonal.spring: Narrow leaves emerge green with possible crimson tints, especially on the fresh flush.
seasonal.summer: Foliage settles to bright or medium green; later growth may carry slightly broader narrow lobes.

size.qualifier: RHS published range with a 20–50-year time to maturity; descriptive text notes eventual development toward about 3 m.

content.cultivation: Use moisture-retentive but well-drained soil in a sheltered site, with full sun to partial shade according to climate. Partial shade and consistent moisture help protect the narrow foliage from scorch; container plants require attentive watering.
content.diagnostic: The defining comparison trait is linearilobum foliage: long strap-like lobes rather than the finely dissected laceleaf structure of RC-002 ‘Seiryu’ or RC-004 ‘Crimson Queen’. Near-names must not be merged on typography alone.
content.confidence: High confidence in accepted name, taxon, leaf-form class and broad seasonal sequence; moderate confidence in the degree of leaf-width change between early and later growth because it is based on a living-collection account rather than a standardized multi-accession study.
content.unresolvedIssue: The informal English nickname and the quantitative extent of early-versus-late leaf dimorphism were not investigated beyond the cited living-collection account.
